name: Dumbbell Pendulum Exercise
summary: A gentle rehabilitation and mobility exercise where the arm hangs relaxed with a light dumbbell while trunk sway drives small circular or pendular motions to mobilize the shoulder joint.

setup: Grasp a very light dumbbell in the hand of the target shoulder.
Hinge at your hips to lean forward until your torso is at a 45- to 90-degree angle, supporting your other hand firmly on a sturdy table, bench, or chair.
Allow the weighted arm to dangle perpendicular to the floor, completely relaxed, letting the light load provide gentle traction to the joint.
steps: Gently sway your hips and torso in small circles or forward-and-back rocking motions to initiate momentum.
Allow the relaxed arm to swing passively in small, controlled circles or arcs driven solely by the movement of your body.
Maintain a completely loose shoulder without actively contracting the deltoid or rotator cuff.
Smoothly reverse the direction of the circles or switch to linear swings as prescribed.
instructions.breathing: Breathe slowly and rhythmically throughout the movement to promote muscular relaxation in the upper body.
cues: Let the arm dangle like a dead weight
Move your body to swing your arm
Keep your neck and shoulder completely relaxed

common_faults.fault: Actively swinging the arm with the shoulder muscles rather than using trunk momentum.
common_faults.correction: Keep the shoulder completely passive and initiate all motion through subtle rocking of your hips and torso.

common_faults.fault: Using too heavy of a dumbbell, causing reflexive muscle guarding.
common_faults.correction: Use minimal load, typically 1 to 5 pounds (0.5 to 2 kg), or perform without weight if any muscle tension is felt.

common_faults.fault: Tensing the neck or hunching the non-working shoulder.
common_faults.correction: Firmly support your upper-body weight on the stable surface and keep your neck relaxed in neutral alignment.

precautions: Do not use heavy resistance; this exercise is designed for joint mobilization and decompression, not strength training.
Stop immediately if you experience sharp or pinching shoulder pain.
